title: Average feature contributions over orders
description: You attribute a prediction by replacing background features in sampled orders.

steps.description: You evaluate the background vector and x, then initialize one contribution per feature. Each sampled permutation starts from a fresh background copy.
You replace one feature at a time and add the resulting output change to phi[j]. Dividing by M averages each feature's contribution across sampled orders.

steps.question: What do all feature changes within one permutation add up to?
steps.answer: They add up to fx minus base_value, apart from numerical rounding. Each change starts where the previous change ended, and the final vector equals x.

steps.description: You form one background vector by averaging up to 200 sampled training rows. You explain test row 5 using 400 sampled permutations.
You compare the baseline plus the summed contributions with the prediction in the final print statement. The supplied recording contains no printed values for this check.
